newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba inaugurates site for anti-embargo monument.
newsitem.headline: Cuba inaugurates site for anti-embargo monument.

text.p: Several hundred youths from Cuba and abroad chanted anti-American rhetoric as Cuba on Tuesday inaugurated the site of a planned a monument of defiance of the 35-year-old U.S. economic embargo.

"Clinton, bastard, remember the Bay of Pigs," shouted the crowd, most them delegates to an international leftist youth festival. The nine-day event, closing later Tuesday, has drawn some 11,000 youths from around the world and focused heavily on condemnation of U.S. "imperialism".

Cuba defeated an invasion of CIA-backed Cuban exiles at the Bay of Pigs in April 1961 and has since defied efforts of successive U.S. administrations to pressure President Fidel Castro's communist governmnent into change.
President Bill Clinton is vilified in Cuba for having toughened the embargo when he approved the so-called Helms-Burton law last year.
Tuesday's ceremony was to erect a large sign a few hundred yards (metres) from the U.S. Interests Section on Havana's sea-front, indicating the site of the anti-embargo monument.
Cuban authorities announced in April they planned to spend some $150,000 of funds raised by foreign solidarity groups on building the 65-foot (20-metre) monument.

Designed by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemayer and expected to be completed by February next year, the monument will consist of a large concrete ring, broken by a 45-foot (14-metre) representation of the Cuban flag rising out of it.
